articles.summary: Meritage Q3 2026: closing revenue fell 17% to $1.2B, adjusted gross margin 17.9%, no Q4 guidance. Land spend $329M, down 38%. Of ~71,800 lots, 69% owned and 31% optioned, against a ~40% off-balance-sheet target. No revolver borrowings.
articles.why_it_matters: Meritage owns 69% of its lots, well short of its 40% off-balance-sheet target, and says land-light deals need enhanced returns to justify their cost, so it is an under-penetrated prospect that will negotiate hard on option pricing.

suggested_update.text: At Sept 30, 2026, 69% of ~71,800 lots were owned and 31% optioned (off-balance-sheet target still ~40%); Q3 land spend $329M, down 38%.

articles.summary: PulteGroup is bringing its Explore by Del Webb brand, aimed at Gen X buyers, to Utah, with the first community at Jordanelle Ridge.
articles.why_it_matters: A product-brand launch in one new market; it says nothing about how PulteGroup funds its land.

articles.summary: Legacy Housing Corporation (NASDAQ: LEGH), a manufactured-home builder, named Darren McCallon chief financial officer.
articles.why_it_matters: Legacy is a manufactured-housing company outside Domain's top-100 site-built customer list, so the CFO change has little bearing on land-bank demand.

articles.summary: Pixar promoted Jonathan Garson to president, succeeding retiring Jim Morris, effective January.
articles.why_it_matters: This is an animation-studio story with no homebuilding link; a keyword search pulled it in.

articles.summary: Starwood Capital and Trez Capital formed a joint venture to lend on single-family residential land, with a $450M seed round and a target of more than $1B of annual originations (Nov 4, 2026).
articles.why_it_matters: A new $1B-a-year source of builder land capital competes directly for Domain's deal flow and pricing. It launched a day after Wafra and Hunt's Strata Land Partners, a sign that institutional capital is crowding into builder land.

articles.summary: Daiwa House cut its FY2026 US homebuilding revenue forecast to ~$4.88B from $5.08B. Sumitomo Forestry cut its 2026 US sales forecast by $776M to $7.01B and closings by 1,455 to 12,705. Both are shifting to cost cuts and synergies.
articles.why_it_matters: The Japanese owners of Stanley Martin, DRB and Tri Pointe are pivoting from acquisitions to capital efficiency, including less capital tied up in land, which could raise their demand for off-balance-sheet lot structures.

articles.summary: A German market-news roundup on Berkshire Hathaway covers GEICO's slowdown, its Lennar stake amid a shareholder suit against Lennar, and a new Bending Spoons position.
articles.why_it_matters: This repeats the Berkshire-Lennar stake story and the Lennar suit, both scored from better sources, and adds nothing for Domain.

articles.summary: A Japanese blog post compares the financial results and stock valuations of Sumitomo Forestry, Daiwa House and Sekisui House.
articles.why_it_matters: This is a stock-valuation blog about the Japanese parents and has no news on their US builders' land or funding.

articles.summary: Fitch downgraded four independent mortgage banks, citing high debt and little room to pay it down from retained earnings in 2027.
articles.why_it_matters: These are mortgage lenders, not homebuilders, so it is only a faint signal of tightening credit around housing.

articles.summary: A templated stock-review piece compares Lennar's Q3 results with those of other homebuilder stocks.
articles.why_it_matters: This is generic stock commentary with nothing on Lennar's land or option strategy.

articles.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's Q3 portfolio changes included selling Bank of America shares and adding to Delta and Lennar.
articles.why_it_matters: This is the same Berkshire-Lennar stake event as the MarketWatch item and adds nothing for Domain.

articles.drop: published outside the last 90 days (NVR Q2 2026 results, dated 2026-07-23 in the URL)

articles.summary: Taylor Morrison broke ground on Esplanade at Cammaray, a 517-acre, roughly 1,200-home community in Lakewood Ranch, Florida, with condos, villas and single-family homes.
articles.why_it_matters: This is a community groundbreaking; it shows Taylor Morrison still adding Sarasota-area lot pipeline but says nothing on how the land is financed.

articles.summary: Berkshire Hathaway nearly doubled its stake in Lennar in the third quarter while cutting some bank holdings, per its latest 13F.
articles.why_it_matters: A larger Berkshire holding is an equity vote of confidence in Lennar's asset-light model, which leans on land bankers like Millrose and Domain, but it changes no funding terms.

articles.summary: KB Home said Albert Z. Praw, its EVP of real estate and business development after 30+ years at the company, retires effective Nov 30, 2026. No successor was named. He will consult on land relations and transactions for up to a year.
articles.why_it_matters: KB Home's top land executive is leaving with no successor named, so Domain should reach his replacement and keep Praw's consulting window open on land deals.

suggested_update.text: Albert Z. Praw, EVP real estate and business development, retires Nov 30, 2026 (announced Nov 16, 2026); no successor named; consulting on land for up to one year.

articles.summary: This is the German MarketScreener version of KB Home's announcement that EVP of real estate Albert Z. Praw retires Nov 30, 2026.
articles.why_it_matters: This is the same event as the kept Zonebourse item and adds no new facts.

articles.summary: A Korean blog analysis of Lennar's 10-K questions its land-light story: owned land cut to about 0.1 years' supply and 98% of lots optioned. It focuses on a $5.6B spin-off and $1.55B of option deposits.
articles.why_it_matters: This is third-party scrutiny of how Lennar accounts for land-bank deposits after the Millrose spin-off, the same theme as the shareholder suit; it is context for Domain's Lennar relationship, not news.

articles.summary: A Lennar shareholder filed a proposed securities class action in the Southern District of Florida against Lennar and two top executives. It alleges they misled investors about financial health and a subsidiary spinoff, including capitalizing land-bank option costs. Class period: Feb 7, 2025 to Oct 2, 2026.
articles.why_it_matters: The suit puts Lennar's accounting for land-bank option costs, and by extension the 2025 Millrose spin-off, under litigation scrutiny. That could change how Lennar and other builders structure and disclose option deals with Domain.

articles.summary: Century Communities' Q3 2026 call: amended revolver raised to $1.2B and extended to November 2030. Full-year guidance lowered. Record 343 communities, 360-370 expected at year-end including 29 from HistoryMaker. Finished lot costs fell 3% sequentially under a low-deposit land control strategy.
articles.why_it_matters: Century, the tenth-largest builder, has more revolver capacity and favors low-deposit land control, so Domain's option pricing has to compete with its own cheap bank line.

suggested_update.text: Revolver amended to $1.2B capacity, maturity extended to November 2030 (disclosed on Q3 2026 call, Oct 29, 2026).
